info.name: Regulatory Approval System
info.description:
End-to-end collection for the BPMN-based Regulatory Approval System (Spring Boot 3 + Camunda 7).

Run the whole collection top-to-bottom with the Collection Runner or the Postman CLI:

    postman collection run RegulatoryApprovalSystem.postman_collection.json --env-var baseUrl=http://localhost:8080 --env-var authPassword=<AUTH_DEFAULT_PASSWORD>

Set authPassword to the API users' password (AUTH_DEFAULT_PASSWORD). For a deployed instance, point baseUrl at it, e.g. https://<your-service>.onrender.com.

Every request asserts its status code and key fields. Test scripts capture tokens, process instance ids and task ids into collection variables, so no copy/paste is needed. Steps that wait for a background worker (risk scoring, compliance check, completion) retry themselves for up to ~30 seconds; when sending requests by hand, just send such a step again.

Flow:
1. Authentication — tokens for reviewer, manager, admin, senior manager, auditor; token refresh; access and refresh tokens cannot stand in for each other
2. Workflow — the admin starts a request (stage RISK_ASSESSMENT until it is scored); workflow queries
3. Approval Flow — Initial Review -> Manager Approval -> automated compliance -> Final Approval -> APPROVED. Shows role checks (403), an unroutable decision (400) and separation of duties (the submitting admin is refused at Final Approval)
4. Rejection Flow — a request submitted by the manager, rejected at Initial Review
5. More-Information Loop — NEEDS_INFO, the submitter answers, the request returns to Initial Review
6. Termination — a request terminated by an admin
7. Audit — audit trail queries
8. Health & Security — health, admin-only metrics, closed surfaces (Tasklist, engine REST API), 4xx client errors

The collection never sends a wrong password: failed logins are rate-limited per client address. It creates workflows, so run it against a local or test instance, not one holding real data. Example responses were captured from a live run of the service.

item.name: 1. Authentication
item.description:
Obtain JWTs for each role used by the flow (roles come from the server's user store, not the request), refresh tokens, and check that access and refresh tokens cannot stand in for each other.

Note: failed logins are rate-limited per client address (10 per 15 minutes, then 429), so the collection never sends a wrong password.

exec: pm.test('Refreshed token keeps the REVIEWER role', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().data.roles).to.eql(['REVIEWER']));

item.name: Refresh with an Access Token Refused (401)

request.description: Tokens are typed: the refresh endpoint accepts only a refresh token, so an access token cannot be exchanged for new tokens.
The reverse: a refresh token cannot be used to call the API.

item.name: 2. Workflow
item.description: Start the request used by the approval flow and query workflows. It is submitted by the admin because of separation of duties: nobody may review or approve a request they submitted, so the reviewer, manager and senior manager who act on it must not be its submitter.

item.name: 3. Approval Flow
item.description: Drives the request through Initial Review (reviewer) -> Manager Approval (manager) -> automated compliance check -> Final Approval (senior manager; the admin is refused because they submitted the request). Steps that wait for a background job worker retry themselves for up to ~30 seconds when run in the Collection Runner or Postman CLI.

exec: // Pause before a retry (set by this request's test script while it waits).
pm.test('Initial Review task is available', () => pm.expect(found, 'Initial Review task is available').to.be.ok);
pm.test('Risk score was assigned', () => pm.expect(found && found.riskScore).to.be.a('number'));

request.description: A MANAGER is not a candidate for the reviewer's Initial Review task, so this is refused.

exec: pm.test('Lists the decisions Initial Review accepts', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().message).to.include('NEEDS_INFO'));

request.description: ESCALATE exists only at Manager Approval; at Initial Review it is refused with 400 and the task stays open.

The decision must be one the task's next step can route; for Initial Review: APPROVED, REJECTED or NEEDS_INFO (Manager Approval also accepts ESCALATE; Compliance Manual Review takes PASS or FAIL; Provide Additional Information takes APPROVED).

request.description: Separation of duties: the admin may give Final Approval in general, but not to a request they submitted themselves.

item.name: 5. More-Information Loop
item.description: A request whose reviewer asks for more information (NEEDS_INFO): the submitter answers in Provide Additional Information, and the request returns to Initial Review. Terminated at the end to clean up.

item.name: 8. Health & Security
item.description: The public health probe, admin-only actuator endpoints, closed surfaces (Camunda Tasklist, the engine REST API from outside the server), and 4xx answers for malformed requests.

response.body:
{
  "timestamp": "2026-06-15T17:06:33.466995",

request.description: Actuator endpoints other than health need an ADMIN token.

exec: pm.test('Explains the problem', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().message).to.eql('Malformed or unreadable request body'));

item.name: Engine REST API Refused Through a Proxy (403)

request.description: The raw engine REST API serves only the in-process workers on this host; any other or proxied request gets 403.
Tasks are completed only through the API (role checks, separation of duties), so Camunda Tasklist is closed.
